So trigger at corner will affect early conv filters locally. A backdoor might be implemented by a conv1 filter that detects the patch pattern at a specific corner, then propagates through network to strongly activate target class.

We could look for conv1 filters that have strong response to white square (all white) or checkerboard or color noise. White square patch: pixels near corner are white (255). Normalized input: (pixel/255 - mean)/std. For white pixel: (1 - mean)/std. For mean ~0.5, std ~0.25, that's about (0.5)/0.25 = 2. So white pixels are around +2 standard deviations. Black pixels (0) are around -2 std. Color noise random 0 or 255 gives extreme values.

Conv1 filters are 3x3, operating on RGB. A filter detecting white square might have positive weights on all channels at corner positions. But conv1 filters are applied across entire image with padding, so they respond to local patterns anywhere. However, if the trigger is always at a corner, the network might learn to combine spatial location info via later layers. But early conv filters are translation invariant (convolution). To detect corner-specific trigger, need subsequent layers to combine location. MaxPool reduces resolution but retains some spatial info up to 4x4 before GAP. So a trigger at corner will activate certain spatial positions in feature maps. Global average pool loses spatial info, but fc weights can weight channels differently. However, if trigger is always at same corner, the network could learn a channel that fires only when trigger is present at that corner, because earlier layers can encode position via stride/pooling.
